issues.description: The problem specification and UML state that getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and adds a new StudentCount class. This changes the method return type and introduces a new type not mentioned in the problem or provided in the template, causing a structural mismatch that will confuse students about the expected signature and return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification: change getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the solution to return an int (the total number of students) instead of StudentCount and remove the StudentCount class, or alternatively update the problem statement and template UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning StudentCount and explicitly introduce StudentCount in the template. Ensure all references (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents, getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) use the same int-based signature.

issues.description: The problem statement / UML and exercise text specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int (primitive total number). The solution implementation instead introduces a StudentCount class and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object. This changes the conceptual representation of the "total number of students" across artifacts and forces students to map an expected int to a custom type (StudentCount) with a getValue() accessor, creating unnecessary confusion about the expected return type and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution so getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a primitive int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove or make StudentCount an internal/unused helper, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the StudentCount type and its API (including getValue()), so students clearly expect and understand the custom type. Prefer (A) to match the stated UML and reduce cognitive load for learners.
